correctness.rationale: Explicit cyclic displacement argument proves the entire stable set for every n≥3. Each n−1 deleted terminal submarket has a unique stable matching, forcing every full-state terminal-only arrival to one of two extremes even after arbitrary previous shocks. Constructive order of arrivals with one auxiliary man reaches shift one via only stable proposal-chain steps; impossibility with zero follows from reachability theorem. Pure-Python independent enumeration for n≤7, full dynamics for n≤6, and n≤50 augmented histories were successfully run. Finite computation supports but does not replace analytical quantification.

value.rationale: Sharp quantitative separation between static stability (n outcomes) and arbitrarily repeated historical evolution (only 2) in the precise market class that generalizes the motivating n=3 obstruction. As n→∞ the reachable proportion vanishes; exactly one invisible historical agent reverses nonreachability for a concrete target. This measures how omission of participant history changes identification, using an all-size theorem and optimal intervention count rather than a parameter-renamed example.
